system.name: tnic
system.one_liner: a trusted NIC architecture providing a minimal, formally verified silicon root-of-trust for building trustworthy distributed systems

components.name: Application code
components.role: user application running on the host that uses tnic's APIs

components.name: User-space buffers
components.role: application-level buffers used by the network library

components.name: Network library
components.role: exposes tnic's programming APIs to applications

components.name: RDMA OS abstractions
components.role: user-space library implementing the software RDMA protocol, intermediating between the application and tnic hardware

components.name: Mapped memory
components.role: memory region mapped for driver/hardware interaction

components.name: Security module
components.role: hardware component implementing trusted network operations

components.name: Attestation kernel
components.role: generates and verifies message attestations for non-equivocation and transferable authentication

components.name: RDMA network stack
components.role: hardware implementation of the IB/RDMA protocol on the SmartNIC

content.key_idea: tnic layers a trusted-network-operations hardware architecture (green) under a software network stack (orange) and a programming-API library (blue), giving applications a verifiable root-of-trust for RDMA networking.
content.reading_order: Top-down through three horizontal layers separated by dashed interface lines: Application code, TNIC software programming API (blue), TNIC software network stack (orange), TNIC hardware architecture (green), down to the network.

evidence: tnic is comprised of three layers (shown in Figure 1)
the tnic hardware architecture (green box) that implements trusted network operations
the tnic network library (blue box) that exposes tnic's programming APIs

summary: tnic is a trusted NIC architecture that builds a minimal, formally verified silicon root-of-trust at the network interface to support trustworthy distributed systems in untrusted cloud environments. This system-overview figure stacks tnic's three layers top-down: application code calls into a blue TNIC (sw) programming API layer (user-space buffers plus a network library) that exposes tnic's programming APIs; below it, an orange TNIC (sw) network stack layer (RDMA OS abstractions and mapped memory) intermediates between the application and the hardware; at the bottom, a green TNIC (hw) architecture layer implements trusted network operations on a SmartNIC through a Security module (with an attestation kernel) and an RDMA network stack, before data reaches the network. Dashed labels mark the interface boundaries between layers (TNIC API, device access interface, TNIC hardware), and a legend distinguishes solid data-path arrows from dashed control-path arrows.
